issues.description: After the Verus update, `lemma_nat_as_parts` no longer proves its nat-valued decomposition because the calc chain does not establish the required intermediate non-overflow/coercion equality.
issues.rationale: With asterinas/verus fixed to 52b20fc504b265409308933340f3b77e0e5128ab, the selected problem snapshot fails exactly at this calc chain: its nat additions are represented with nested `clip(nat, ...)`, and the asserted equality is not established. The immediate repair rewrites the decomposition through explicitly non-negative `int` terms, proves the integer sum, and only then casts back to `nat`; the same target then verifies successfully.
issues.source_evidence: after/lock-protocol-rcu/src/mm/page_table/mod.rs:935-945 contains the failing nat-valued calc chain. Historical execution reports an assertion failure at line 935 with `455 verified, 1 errors`. Repair commit 04bbe66ef7f7b7bae8d928570387e4f7964739e2 changes this lemma to an explicit int-sum bridge; the identical command then reports `470 verified, 0 errors`.
issues.verification: historical Verus executed. Pinned asterinas/verus 52b20fc504b265409308933340f3b77e0e5128ab and Z3 4.12.5; `cargo xtask verify --targets lock-protocol-rcu` fails on the problem SHA with 455 verified/1 error and passes on the immediate repair SHA with 470 verified/0 errors. No archived CI artifact identifies the author's exact Verus SHA, so the verifier is reproducibly selected as the latest origin/1.91.0 commit before the immutable problem commit time.
